answer: Per-epoch nullifiers make sybils expensive. Each real principal holds one anonymous jade credential with a secret s; each epoch it derives N = H(s, epoch), and the ledger rejects a repeat. Clone one operator into fifty agents and all collide on one tag, like climbers sharing a mesa: only the first claim clears. A zero-knowledge proof validates it without exposing s. Yarrow cast once yields one omen; a nullifier cannot be recast, and fresh ones need new credentials no amount of compute can forge. A fake account now costs a scarce real principal: aliases are endless, nullifiers are not.
